A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BiPS research. All 15 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, references, and supplementary Sections 6–8, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original BiPS training and evaluation results, component and curriculum ablations, coefficient sensitivity, and qualitative cases, including the supplementary GRPO comparison.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds evaluation of BiPS on Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking in supplementary Section 7.2 and Table 7.

M1.justification: The programmatic view construction, consistency and separation objectives, and two-stage BiPS curriculum remain unchanged. Applying BiPS to Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking adds an experimental configuration, not a new method component.

E1.justification: The ECD-derived chart training, optional ViRL39k training, and chart/general-reasoning benchmark coverage are retained. The Qwen3 experiment uses the existing benchmark suite; natural-image and maze training extensions are proposed as future work, not evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 adds Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking and its GRPO-trained counterpart as comparators for BiPS on that backbone. The Qwen2.5 GRPO comparison now appearing in Table 1 already existed in v1 Table 7 and is relocated evidence.

E3.justification: Section 7.2 adds a thinking-backbone evaluation using 13K chart samples, specified decoding settings, and benchmark-specific prompts. The base model receives the best score over presence penalties 1.2 and 1.5, while the fine-tuned setting uses 1.2. The original Qwen2.5 evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 7.1 adds a concrete chart-view construction case in Figure 7, illustrating the evidence that must be retained or removed. Section 7.2 adds qualitative observations about OCR degradation and prompt mitigation, without a quantified mitigation ablation. Existing component, curriculum, masking, and coefficient analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The eight training rollouts remain unchanged; the new decoding-parameter sweep is not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds a complete eight-benchmark result set for Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking, GRPO, and BiPS. Table 7 reports CharXiv scores of 53.0, 54.3, and 58.1 respectively, but MathVista scores of 81.0, 80.4, and 80.4, showing mixed transfer relative to the base model. These are new-configuration results, not improvements over v1 scores. Existing Qwen2.5 results are retained, with the relocated GRPO row additionally reporting a 50.7 average.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives and definitions in Equations 1–5 are unchanged, and no theorem, proof, or derivation is added. The revised shortcut-learning explanation is conceptual prose rather than a formal mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about bidirectional perceptual shaping, data efficiency, generalization, and absence of additional inference overhead. The headline Qwen2.5 average improvements of 7.3 and 8.2 points are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.2.2 expands the shortcut explanation to include surrounding OCR text as well as language priors. New Section 7.2 acknowledges OCR degradation and more limited transfer on the thinking model, proposes prompt mitigation, and discusses multi-domain extensions as future work.

D1.justification: Table 1 newly states that baselines were reproduced using VLMEvalKit; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun. Section 7.2 supplies decoding parameters, the presence-penalty selection procedure, MMStar prompt cleanup, and the OCR-oriented MathVerse system prompt. Existing training details and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to the Qwen3-VL technical report and Imagine While Reasoning in Space. Its extensibility discussion connects BiPS to segmentation-assisted natural-image processing and procedural mazes. The principal related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The former supplementary GRPO discussion moves into Section 4.2, while supplementary Section 7.2 now covers Qwen3 settings, interpretation, and extensibility. Other changes include the expanded case discussion, revised shortcut explanation, and Microsoft Research Asia affiliation; most existing prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: The old supplementary GRPO comparison is consolidated into Table 1, a new Qwen3 comparison uses Table 7, and Figure 7 adds an original/preserved/ablated chart illustration. Table placement and appendix prompt layout shift, while existing diagrams, plots, and case figures remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added Qwen3 comparison broadens validation beyond the original backbone, while explicit decoding details and discussion of OCR degradation and weaker transfer improve transparency. Moving the existing GRPO control into the main results also improves accessibility. The gain is incremental: the core method and original findings are unchanged, the new transfer results are mixed, and OCR mitigation remains qualitatively documented without uncertainty estimates.
